constraints.text: Remittance dependence. Guatemala took in US$8.431 billion in remittances between January and April 2026, 53.2% of the three Northern Triangle countries' total. From January 2026 a 1% US tax applies to transfers made in cash, money orders or cashier's cheques, so the economy rests on a corridor Washington can tax.

constraints.text: Congress, the judiciary and the attorney general. Wikipedia records strong opposition to the Arevalo government from the judiciary, Congress and the establishment. The attorney general serves a four-year term and can be removed only for a conviction for an offence committed in office, so the chief prosecutor is not the president's to dismiss.

paradoxes.text: The deal that buys US goodwill makes Mexico the aggrieved neighbour. Guatemala received about 2,300 Mexicans deported from the US in 2026 and kept them for less than 24 hours; Mexico's foreign ministry opposed the practice, so the border partner now protests the transit country.

grand_strategy.reading: Guatemala under Arevalo trades migration services for US money and security, and keeps Taiwan as a diplomatic card it has not spent on Beijing. Its economy is remittances, a corridor Washington taxes and can tighten, so the deportation deal is a lever it cannot easily refuse. The attorney general and the courts, shielded from quick removal, are the constraint that decides how far the president can move.

stances.note: Mirror of the Taiwan card's stance toward Guatemala (data/stances/TWN.yaml, graded B there), written here as a reciprocal one grade lower: the same two 2025 press reports on Arevalo's Taipei visit, plus the 1933 date from Wikipedia (tier 4 pointer). Partner by recognition, bond affinity. No source read shows a Guatemalan move toward Beijing; the China pressure is on Taipei, not on Guatemala's own posture.

stances.note: Guatemala's claim to the territory of Belize, written by hand from this side as the mirror of the Belize card (data/stances/BLZ.yaml). The 1859 Wyke-Aycinena treaty, which Guatemala negotiated, recognised British sovereignty over the region; Guatemala later renewed the claim, and in 1999 shifted back to inheriting Spanish and Federal Republic of Central America rights (Wikipedia index, tier 4). Grade read from the claim, not from the rhetoric. Bond grievance: an open historical wound, the claim itself. Confidence C: tier 4 pointer only; no Guatemalan government statement was read.

stances_toward.note: The rival side of the territorial dispute. Belize's own territory is own_territory on its side and is not written as a self-stance. Rival, not adversary: Belize has sent the claim to the ICJ and reads Guatemala as a legal opponent, not as a state whose existence is in question (Wikipedia index, tier 4). Bond grievance: the open claim is the wound. The mirror of Guatemala's claimed_territory is written in data/stances/GTM.yaml. stances_toward.note: Rewritten on 2026-10-16 from Mexico's side (replaces the provisional reciprocal of the GTM card). Border and migration partner with friction: in August 2026 President Arevalo confirmed that about 2,300 Mexicans deported from the US had transited Guatemala in 2026, held under 24 hours; Mexico's foreign ministry opposed the practice and a US spokesperson called them people in transit (KJZZ, 20 Aug 2026, read from a search summary). The sovereignty line is the same as against Washington; the partner grade holds because the quarrel is about transit, not about the state. The since date is the August 2026 incident, not the start of the partnership, which is unsourced. Bond none, our reading. Guatemala also voiced concerns similar to Mexico's over the 3 Jan 2026 strike on Venezuela (Fox News report of reactions), a shared line on intervention. Confidence C.
